 Love lessons with Seo Kang-jun and Ahn Eun-jin 
 The stars of Prime Video’s A Love Other Than Yours get candid about temptation, relationships, and taking love for granted.
 “They loved each other so deeply that, at some point, they forgot just how much they loved each other.”
 Ten years is a long time to love someone. You’ve seen each other at your best and worst, know each other’s habits by heart and can probably predict what the other will say before they say it. But does knowing someone that well mean you truly understand them? Or can familiarity get in the way of seeing who they’ve become?
 That’s the question at the centre of A Love Other Than Yours , Prime Video’s new Korean drama. Seo Kang-jun plays Namgung Ho and Ahn Eun-jin is Lee Mi-do, a couple whose decade together hits a turning point when Ho starts thinking about marriage. Mi-do, a film director stuck in a career slump, is busy falling for another man. Their answer is a dangerous pact to face temptation head-on. Jealousy, tangled feelings and some uncomfortable truths follow.
 Photo Courtesy of Prime Video. 
 For Seo, the answer to whether love can last beyond the initial excitement comes down to how much you value the other person. “In a long-term relationship, love can be felt through excitement, deep trust, and comfort,” he says. “But I think another important question is how much you value that person.” Sometimes, he suggests, it is only when you imagine life without someone that you realise just how much they mean to you.
 Ahn, meanwhile, sees Ho and Mi-do’s relationship as a cautionary tale about taking love for granted. “I think they loved each other so deeply that, at some point, they forgot just how much they loved each other,” she says.
 It is a familiar trap: assuming that because you’ve been together for years, you already know everything there is to know about your partner. Ahn says working on the series made her reflect on how easily those assumptions can damage a relationship. Seo had a similar realisation while playing Ho. “In reality, they didn’t actually know what the other person was truly thinking or feeling inside,” he explains.
 So, is their decade together enough to keep them together? That was one of the questions Seo found himself asking when he first read the script. “Why can’t these two break up , no matter how much they fight? Is it simply because of love?” he recalls. For him, understanding the history and emotions beneath their relationship was key to understanding Ho.
 Ahn, on the other hand, found herself wondering what would happen to the characters after the drama ended. She was particularly drawn to the way they gradually move towards a healthier, more mature understanding of love—even if getting there means confronting some difficult truths.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by GRAZIA Malaysia (@grazia.my) 
 And perhaps that is what makes A Love Other Than Yours so relatable. Relationships rarely come with a clear answer when things get complicated. Sometimes, the harder question isn’t whether you still love someone, but whether you’re truly seeing them for who they are today.
 A Love Other Than Yours is available on Prime Video .
